test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 98 min and 28 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 42 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the cistern take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 98, 28, 42) = 588 units.

Efficiency of **Pipe 1** = 588 ÷ 98 = 6 units/min.

Efficiency of **Pipe 2** = 588 ÷ 28 = 21 units/min.

Combined Efficiency (All 3 pipes) = 588 ÷ 42 = 14 units/min.

Efficiency of **Emptying Pipe** = (6 + 21) − 14 = 13 units/min.

Time to empty = 588 ÷ 13 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 588/13 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by Inlet A = 98 min, Inlet B = 28 min, Combined (A+B−C) = 42 min.

⇒ Total positive efficiency (A + B) = 6 + 21 = 27 units/min

⇒ Net efficiency with outlet pipe = 14 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of Outlet Pipe C = (A + B) − Net efficiency

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe C = 27 − 14 = 13 units/min

⇒ Time taken by Outlet Pipe C alone = Total Capacity ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time = 588 ÷ 13 min

**∴ The correct answer is 588/13 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Inlet pipes are treated as **positive work** (+) and outlet/leakage pipes are treated as **negative work** (−).

Total Work Formula

Total Work (Capacity) = Time taken × Efficiency. For multiple pipes, Net Efficiency = ∑(Individual Efficiencies).

Unitary Method for Time

If a pipe fills in 'x' hours and another empties in 'y' hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y).</p
